transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-09-10 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Sarah Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Alex Rivera (Cypress - Lead ML Eng), Priya Shah (Cypress - DevOps Lead), Marcus Lee (Cypress - Eng Manager)

Summary: quick hands-on lab to validate SDK auth flows (Python + TS), how to wire up KMS, and deploy in private VPC. Focus on sample snippets, console steps, and security/ops questions.

[00:00] Sarah Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll give a quick lab -- hi Alex, Priya, Marcus, uh Daniel and I will run through the SDK quickstarts and the VPC/KMS bits. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Alex Rivera: Good, thanks. We've got a short window today, about 45-ish, hope that's fine.
[00:10] Daniel Cho: Yeah absolutely, we'll try to be tidy. Quick agenda: Python quickstart, TypeScript example, auth (KMS/HSM), console bits for VPC/private control plane, then Q&A and next steps.
[00:21] Priya Shah: Top priority for us is that keys never leave our KMS and we need audit logs into our SIEM. Also want to check latency on Dedicated vs hosted.
[00:30] Sarah Martinez: Noted. We'll show both, and Daniel will point out tradeoffs. Also we'll link the security whitepaper after the call.
[00:36] Marcus Lee: For timelines, we want a pilot in the next two weeks if possible.
[00:40] Daniel Cho: Cool, that aligns well. I'll start with Python. I'm sharing my screen — hope the audio isn't too laggy.
[00:46] [screen share noise]
[00:50] Daniel Cho: So here's the repo: examples/python-quickstart. First step is pip install redwood-inference-sdk, then export REDWOOD_API_KEY or use workload identity. Typical snippet — import, client = Redwood(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')) — uh transcription note: sometimes env var name is REDWOOD_KEY in older samples, ignore that.
[01:12] Alex Rivera: Wait, about workload identity, we run on GKE; can you show the GCP workload identity flow again?
[01:18] Daniel Cho: Yep. In GKE you can use workload identity to mint short lived credentials that map to a Redwood service account via OIDC. We have a doc, but the gist is: annotate the pod, configure IAM, and the SDK will pick up credentials via the metadata server. There's a tiny server side exchange where our control plane validates the OIDC token.
[01:38] Priya Shah: And does that mean keys are stored in Redwood? We need HSM-backed keys only in our KMS.
[01:44] Sarah Martinez: Good question. For private deployments you can bring-your-own-KMS and BYO-HSM on-prem, so the keys never live in Redwood. For hosted API, you can integrate with customer KMS using envelope encryption — we still may have ephemeral keys but ciphertext is controlled by your KMS.
[01:58] Alex Rivera: Envelope encryption — can you walk through a code example with Python quickly?
[02:03] Daniel Cho: Sure. Example: before sending prompt you call KMS.encrypt to wrap a per-request symmetric key, then pass the wrapped key in the SDK init: client = Redwood(api_key=..., wrapped_key=wrapped_key). On private deployment the control plane unwraps with your KMS provider. In hosted mode we do a lightweight transform but we store only ciphertext; there's a whitepaper with diagrams.
[02:30] [00:02:30] Sarah Martinez: Note — some of the terminology in our docs is 'wrap-key' which sometimes gets transcribed as 'wrap-key' or 'wrap-ke' in older videos.
[02:38] Alex Rivera: Okay that helps. On the SDK itself, what about TypeScript differences — token handling or streaming? We use Node for our backend.
[02:45] Daniel Cho: Good point. The TS SDK mirrors Python but streaming uses EventSource or WebSockets. Auth is identical if you use workload identity vs env var. Example, const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, kmsWrappedKey: wrappedKey }); then client.generateStream(...). The biggest gotcha is Node's TLS settings when inside a VPC private endpoint — you might need to set CA bundles if you use a private CA.
[03:12] Priya Shah: That's important — our cluster uses a internal CA. Can Redwood accept a customer CA for the private control plane?
[03:18] Sarah Martinez: Yes for Redwood Private we support customer CA termination and mutual TLS in the private control plane. We'll share the exact setup steps.
[03:26] Marcus Lee: For latency testing, we'd like to run a couple of 512-token prompts with KV cache warm and cold. How do we run that on Dedicated trial?
[03:35] Daniel Cho: We can provision a small Dedicated pod for you for a week. I'll propose two run modes: warm cache where you pre-seed the KV cache using a tracer endpoint, and cold start as a baseline. We'll also show batching behavior in the Optimize tab.
[03:49] [03:49] Alex Rivera: Nice. Are there any constraints around batch size for our use case — we're doing ~200 rps at peak.
[03:55] Daniel Cho: With Dedicated you can tune the max batch size and latency SLO. For 200 rps you might need autoscale policies — we'll suggest starting with 2 pods and 128-token batch targets, then adjust. The Console shows per-model token breakdown and cost per token so you can see economics.
[04:17] Sarah Martinez: On Optimize, we can show quantization recommendations per model. For example, if you pick a 7B model we recommend int8 for batchy workloads; for low-latency you might want 4-bit with slightly worse quality — Daniel, can you share the quant charts?
[04:31] Daniel Cho: Yep, pull those now. [screen] This chart is model latency vs quantization. Keep in mind QA test prompts might see a 2-3% drop in accuracy with aggressive quant but big cost gains.
[04:48] Priya Shah: We will need to run our eval suite; can Redwood run nightly evals against rollouts so we catch regressions?
[04:55] Sarah Martinez: Yes, we have a rollout policy tied to evals; you can pin model versions and require eval pass thresholds to promote canaries.
[05:05] Alex Rivera: On the logging and audit side — does the control plane expose tokenized logs or raw prompts? We need PII never to be stored.
[05:12] Daniel Cho: Default is to redact prompt content for hosted tenancy unless you opt-in. With Private deployment, logs stay in your VPC and you control retention and forwarding. Audit logs include call metadata, latency, and redaction flags.
[05:25] [05:25] Sarah Martinez: Note: sometimes transcript shows 'redact' as 'reacted' in auto transcripts — ignore that.
[05:30] Marcus Lee: Thanks. Let's walk through a quick live TypeScript snippet — can you run a small generate and stream back to the console so we can see the event stream shape?
[05:38] Daniel Cho: Running now. Code: const stream = await client.generateStream({ model: 'rw-compat-7b', input: 'Summarize recent transactions...' }); stream.on('data', chunk => console.log(chunk.text)); You'll see chunked partials and a final message with usage tokens.
[05:58] [05:58] [streaming noise] 
[06:06] Alex Rivera: The streaming chunks look good. For telemetry, can we get per-request tracing IDs to tie back to our logs?
[06:12] Daniel Cho: Yes, every request returns a request_id and we support attaching a customer_trace_id header so you can correlate.
[06:20] Priya Shah: On SSO/SSM, we use Okta and need RBAC for both Console and API keys. How granular is Redwood's RBAC?
[06:28] Sarah Martinez: We support SSO via SAML/OIDC and role-based policies for Console and API key scopes. You can limit keys to read-only or inference only, and issue short-lived tokens via the SDK.
[06:39] Alex Rivera: Any gotchas with rotating keys and CI/CD? We want automated key rotation without downtime.
[06:44] Daniel Cho: Use ephemeral tokens via your KMS and workload identity, or use our short-lived API keys with rotation hooks. We also have an onboarding script that updates secrets in Vault/Secret Manager.
[06:55] [06:55] Sarah Martinez: I'll add that onboarding script to the repo we share.
[07:00] Marcus Lee: On the cost side, what's the expected tokens per second cost delta between hosted and Dedicated for a 7B int8 model?
[07:08] Daniel Cho: Ballpark: hosted might be 10-15% higher per-token because of multi-tenant overhead, but Dedicated reduces per-token cost especially at scale due to caching and batch tuning. We'll include a cost model spreadsheet.
[07:24] Alex Rivera: Good. Ok, can we pivot to VPC setup? Priya needs the exact steps to open private endpoints and route DNS.
[07:31] Daniel Cho: In Private you get a private control plane endpoint — you peering or VPC connector. Steps: 1) Create VPC peering or Private Service Connect, 2) Add route table entries, 3) Configure firewall rules to our control plane subnets, 4) Upload your CA if mutual TLS is required. We'll send a checklist.
[07:55] Priya Shah: For audit forwarding, can we push to Splunk/Datadog via syslog or HTTP webhook?
[08:01] Sarah Martinez: Both; we support webhook sinks and direct Splunk HEC integration. For high-volume forwarding we recommend a buffered gateway in your VPC.
[08:12] Alex Rivera: Great. Any compliance docs for SOC2, ISO that you can share now?
[08:16] Sarah Martinez: Yes, I'll attach SOC2 Type II summary and our ISO-27001 cert link after the call.
[08:23] [08:23] Daniel Cho: Quick note on one more thing — KV cache priming. If you have conversational state you can warm the cache using the /prime endpoint and then run warm latency test.
[08:34] Priya Shah: How do we guarantee that primed cache data doesn't persist beyond retention window? We need auto-eviction.
[08:40] Daniel Cho: You can set TTL on cached entries; Dedicated gives you full control of retention policies and a manual purge endpoint.
[08:49] Alex Rivera: Perfect. Time check — we've got about 35 minutes left? Wait, transcript timestamps and meeting duration are a bit off. Anyway...
[08:58] Sarah Martinez: We're at 22 mins in the recording, roughly. We'll keep moving. Next, let's demo the Console 'Optimize' tab for batching recommendations.
[09:06] [screen switching]
[09:10] Daniel Cho: Here: Optimize -> Workloads -> Recommendations. You can upload a trace file and we'll suggest batch sizes, quantization, and whether caching will help. Click 'run suggestion' for 'retail-chat' workload.
[09:24] [09:24] Alex Rivera: Hmm the suggestion says increase batch to 64 for cost best-effort. That seems optimistic for our latency SLAs.
[09:31] Daniel Cho: You can specify latency SLO and we'll produce Pareto options. For example, choose 200ms SLO and it narrows to lower batch sizes.
[09:40] Priya Shah: Any pre-built governance templates? We have to comply with finance-specific controls.
[09:46] Sarah Martinez: We have templates for restricted retention and audit-forwarding; will include a 'finance-ready' checklist in the doc pack.
[09:55] Marcus Lee: Quick question on models — can we bring our own model or fine-tune a public model and host it on Redwood Private?
[10:02] Daniel Cho: Yes, BYOM supported in Private: you'll provide the model artifact and we run a validation step. Fine-tuning is currently via our partner pipeline; we can discuss a path to production.
[10:12] Alex Rivera: Sounds good. For the pilot, what's the minimum resource commitment?
[10:17] Sarah Martinez: For Dedicated trial we can do a 1-week proof with sample capacity reserved—no long-term commit needed for trial. For Private we have a minimum platform fee but we can scope a short pilot in your VPC.
[10:29] Daniel Cho: I'm going to drop a link to the repo and the quickstart snippets in the chat now. [link: github.com/redwood-inference/examples/integrator-lab]
[10:39] Alex Rivera: Got it. Thanks.
[10:42] Priya Shah: One last security nit: do you support customer-managed HSM (CloudHSM) for key wrapping?
[10:48] Sarah Martinez: Yes, we integrate with CloudHSM and Azure Key Vault HSM-backed keys for Private. For hosted we support envelope encryption with customer KMS providers.
[10:59] [10:59] Daniel Cho: Okay wrapping up, suggested next steps: we'll send code samples, security docs, cost model, and propose dates for benchmarking. Any objections?
[11:10] Alex Rivera: No objections. We'll review docs and schedule internal stakeholders.
[11:14] Marcus Lee: Let's aim for the week of Sep 22 for benchmark.
[11:18] Sarah Martinez: Great, we'll follow up with calendar invite and a proposed dedicated trial window.
[11:23] [11:23] Priya Shah: Thanks everyone.
[11:25] Sarah Martinez: Thanks all. Meeting adjourned.

Action items recap:
- Daniel: Python & TS KMS code samples; due 2025-09-17
- Sarah: VPC runbook, SOC2 & ISO docs; due 2025-09-12
- Alex: Confirm stakeholders and sample dataset; due 2025-09-19

End transcript.
